key_idea: Only 8 cities matter: run Dijkstra from city 1 and from each distinct ball city, then try all orders of visiting the balls (at most 7! = 5040).
sketch: Deduplicate the ball cities, run up to 8 Dijkstras on the 2e5-edge graph to build a pairwise distance table, then enumerate permutations starting from city 1 and take the cheapest total. O(8 m log n + 7!*7). Pitfalls: several balls may share a city or lie in city 1, zero-weight edges are allowed, output -1 if any ball city is unreachable, and use 64-bit distances for safety.
